channel.title: nexusEVnews
channel.description: Independent EV and renewable energy news, curated daily. Electric vehicles, solar, battery tech, and charging infrastructure.

item.title: What the Options List Leaves Out
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Two BMW X3 reports, the most powerful Golf GTI yet, Tesla's October Roadster event and a desert Rivian charging stop show what no order form covers.

item.title: Same Forecourt, Different Fuel
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Norway's fuel stations are turning into charging stops. A rear-drive GTI, a hydrogen X5, a Mach-E past zero and India's solar push follow the same pattern.

item.title: Build It First, or Sell a Backup Plan
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: China built EV infrastructure before demand. Long Beach wants to do the same for floating wind, while Volvo sells a big-battery hedge to doubtful drivers.

item.title: The Best EV Numbers This Week Belong to Cars You Can't Buy
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Volkswagen claims a drag coefficient world record, a student solar racer already beats it, and this week's Volvo and Skoda reviews show the showroom gap.

item.title: Nobody Agrees What Counts as a Chinese Car. The Price Does.
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Electrifying's podcast asked listeners where a car stops being Chinese. Today's Twingo, Mazda and Volkswagen reviews show the answer already has a number attached to it.

item.title: The Warranty Outlives the Company
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A 25 year solar warranty is only worth the installer still being in business, and four other videos ask the same question of a battery plant and a discontinued SUV.

item.title: The Most Range Finished Last
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: The longest-range SUV in Edmunds' eight-car test came eighth, and four other videos show where the argument moved.

item.title: The Self-Starter Test
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A starter motor ended the electric car's easiest sales pitch in 1912, and today's videos test which EV advantages could vanish as quickly.

item.title: The Repeat Is the Review
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Most car verdicts rest on one drive or one run, and today's videos show how often a second measurement changes the answer.

item.title: The Barrier Was Never the Battery
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Oslo makes charging cheaper than parking, CATL drops its minimum order to 600 cells, and a 98 year old buys a Model Y to stop watching intersections.

item.title: Shape Beats Capacity
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Audi kept the ID.3's battery and spent its engineering on drag instead. A house with 30 kilowatt hours of storage outlasted one with 68. The same lesson, twice.

item.title: Delivered, Then Measured
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A two-seat robotaxi on its first public days, a Model Y L that beats its own EPA figure, and an R2 owner running a fifth below rated efficiency three weeks in.

item.title: The Price of a Mile Is Coming Apart
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A £154,000 Range Rover, a $37,500 Fiat with 149 miles of range, and a sodium cell reported at about $51 a kilowatt hour, all in the same week.

item.title: Built to Be Corrected
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Wind turbine blades that leave the factory already carrying repairs, a Polestar that gets its rear window back, and three premium EVs throttled by the chargers rather than by the cars.

item.title: Nobody Was Argued Into It
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Kenyan petrol up 50 percent, Thai showrooms filling with duty-free Chinese imports, Japan with almost no chargers, and a $29,990 Chevrolet that went 243 miles.

item.title: The Gap Between Two Owners
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A plug-in hybrid study where the driver moves the emissions figure, three days of measured solar on one parked car, and two home batteries waiting on Britain.

item.title: The Self-Driving Story Nobody Is Telling
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: The autonomy debate is all horse race. But for millions of people who cannot drive, a car that drives itself is the keys, handed back. Why Rivian's road to Level 4 matters more than the spec sheet, and the one thing it still has to get right.

item.title: We Built the Tracker We Wish Existed When We Were Waiting for Our R1s
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: People were reading website source code to find out when their Rivian was coming. Forum signatures listed Guide contact dates like military service records. We are not doing that again for the R2. The Rivian R2 Delivery Tracker is live.

item.title: Two Batteries, One Hitch, and the Case for All-Electric Glamping
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: The Lightship AE1 carries its own 69 kWh battery and 80 kW motor to neutralize trailer drag on the tow vehicle. Paired with a Rivian, the real-world efficiency numbers are hard to argue with. This is what all-electric glamping looks like when the hardware actually works.

item.title: Atlanta, Rivian, and the Quiet Coincidence
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: Atlanta has a failing air quality grade and a Rivian plant on its doorstep. A hypothetical about what one city could do with the electric mobility infrastructure that already exists — R2 autonomous taxis, ALSO cargo quads, e-bikes, and ZTL-style restricted zones — and what the health data says the stakes actually are. Includes data from the HEI lockdown air quality study (Chen et al., 2025) and the American Lung Association's 2025 Atlanta air quality report.
